articles.title: Home Assistant removes bad readings without erasing the whole history
articles.dek: A preview lets people select a time range to delete while keeping the rest of a statistic.
body: Home Assistant adds a way to remove a bad stretch of recorded measurements while keeping the rest of the history. A new dialog in the statistics table previews the selected time range before deleting its statistics.

This is especially useful for averages such as temperature, whose recorded statistics cannot be adjusted like cumulative totals. Previously, removing an erroneous reading meant deleting the entire statistic. Paulus Schoutsen supplies the matching data handling and interface.

pullRequests.title: Add dialog to delete statistics in a time range
Add time range to recorder/clear_statistics

media.alt: Home Assistant dialog for deleting statistics within a selected time range

articles.title: ESPHome turns an ESP32 into a Thread border router
articles.dek: Makers gain an experimental Wi-Fi bridge for Thread devices, with built-in or separate radios.
body: ESPHome adds an experimental way to use an ESP32 as a Thread border router, connecting a Thread network through Wi-Fi. ESP32-C5 and C6 boards use their built-in radio; other Wi-Fi ESP32 variants can use a separate radio connected by serial wiring.

Pawel Puterla tested the built-in-radio path on an ESP32-C6 for two weeks without a restart or router hang. An ESP32-S3 with a separate radio hung two or three times over about three weeks, so that path needs particular care. The work includes setup guidance and is his first contribution to ESPHome.

OpenThread configurations now require ESP-IDF 5.5.5 or newer, including ordinary Thread devices. That version has already been the default for several releases; makers who pinned an older version need to remove or raise the pin.

pullRequests.title: [openthread] Add ESP32 OpenThread Border Router support
[openthread] Add ESP32 OpenThread Border Router documentation

articles.title: Sendspin streams the sound playing on a Mac or Linux computer
articles.dek: The command-line player captures system audio, with safeguards against sending its own playback back to the server.
body: Sendspin’s command-line player adds a way to send the sound a Mac or Linux computer is already playing to a compatible server. People can capture the default audio output or choose one output device, extending the earlier microphone and line-in support to audio from applications.

On macOS 14.2 or later, the capture excludes Sendspin’s own playback to avoid feeding it back to the server. The computer needs System Audio Recording permission; a silent capture triggers a warning if permission appears to be missing. Chris tested system sounds, individual outputs and changing the output’s sample rate on macOS 26.

On Linux, the player uses PipeWire or PulseAudio and follows changes to the default output. It warns when the capture could include the player’s own sound. Tests covered capture and recovery with virtual audio outputs; this is a command-line capability rather than a new graphical control.

Add a loopback input on macOS through a process tap

articles.title: Music Assistant restores full SoundCloud tracks after a format change
articles.dek: The provider accepts SoundCloud’s newer audio streams instead of rejecting songs or settling for previews.
body: Music Assistant restores playback for SoundCloud tracks that no longer offer an MP3 stream. SoundCloud’s newer streams use AAC audio; the connection previously rejected them, leaving tracks unplayable or offering only a thirty-second preview.

BeeSouul adds the missing format and prefers a full stream over a preview, while retaining MP3 where a full copy exists. In the contributor’s thirty-track search, twenty-two tracks had no MP3 version and the remaining eight offered MP3 previews only. A test using a free SoundCloud account on a Raspberry Pi 4 played previously failing tracks in full.
This is BeeSouul’s first contribution to Music Assistant’s server, reviewed by Marvin Schenkel.

pullRequests.title: Soundcloud: play tracks only served as AAC (HLS)

articles.title: Home Assistant brings Android sleep stages onto dashboards
articles.dek: Health Connect supplies sleep timing and individual stages without treating missing data as zero.
body: Home Assistant’s Android app adds sleep start and end times alongside the duration of light, deep and REM sleep and the other stages recorded in Health Connect. The existing sleep-duration sensor also carries the ordered stage timeline, including each stage’s start and end.

The sensors read the latest sleep session supplied through Health Connect, regardless of which compatible app recorded it. Separate sessions are not combined, and stages the source does not provide remain unavailable instead of appearing as zero. The existing total sleep-duration reading is unchanged. Kruse Ludington supplies the sensors and guide in his first contributions to Home Assistant’s Android app and Companion documentation.

pullRequests.title: Add Health Connect sleep stages sensors
Document Health Connect sleep stage sensors

articles.title: ESPHome measures brightness, colour and light for growing plants
articles.dek: Calibrated spectral sensors add useful light measurements beyond raw colour-band readings.
body: ESPHome adds a shared driver for AS7341, AS7343 and TCS3448 spectral sensors, giving makers measurements of brightness, colour temperature and the light useful to plants. It also reports individual colour bands, an RGB colour value and how close a reading is to saturation.

Anton Viktorov combines the sensor support with calibration that makes readings at different exposures comparable. In his diffuse-daylight testing, the two tested sensors measured brightness within about 15% of an uncalibrated handheld light meter. Absolute accuracy depends on the optics and calibration of each installation.

Moving from the older AS7341 driver changes its raw counts because that driver read the two bytes in the wrong order. Existing calculations based on those counts need attention when changing to the new driver.

articles.title: Home Assistant reads paired Powerwalls directly over the local network
articles.dek: Teslemetry refreshes live values every five seconds, while cloud connectivity still governs availability.
body: Home Assistant’s Teslemetry connection reads live Powerwall values directly from a paired gateway every five seconds and configuration settings every thirty seconds. If the gateway cannot be reached, the connection falls back to cloud values.

Local readings extend the direct command route introduced earlier. A successful setting change keeps its requested value until the relevant local or cloud source reports again, preventing an intervening update from briefly undoing it on screen. Entity availability still follows the Teslemetry stream, so this does not establish an offline operating mode.

articles.title: Music Assistant lets owners approve unpaired Sendspin audio inputs
articles.dek: Devices with an input ask for a fresh setup choice, with pairing and input permission kept separate.
body: Music Assistant lets an unpaired Sendspin device send audio after its owner explicitly approves the input. Previously, connecting without pairing disabled the input entirely, so a device’s line-in appeared only after pairing.

Devices with an input show a setup choice: connect unpaired with the input, connect without it, or pair the device. Existing devices ask once after updating because an earlier saved setting did not establish explicit approval. The input can be enabled or disabled later, and disabling an active input stops playback immediately.
Maxim Raznatovski supplies the Music Assistant change and the corresponding permission support in Sendspin’s Python server. Marvin Schenkel reviewed the Music Assistant work.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows how far cloud backup uploads have progressed
articles.dek: Dropbox and Azure gain percentages, and the overall bar follows the slowest destination.
body: Home Assistant’s backup progress bar fills as uploads advance instead of only pulsing. With several destinations, it follows the slowest upload so a copy already written locally does not make the whole backup look further along.

Dropbox and Azure Storage also begin reporting their upload progress. Dropbox’s percentage can lead the actual transfer by one buffered chunk of up to 16 MB; Azure uploads of 64 MB or less report only completion.

Update screens explain when a Home Assistant backup is creating, uploading or restoring and temporarily disable updates until it finishes. That warning covers backups started through Home Assistant; other installation failures are displayed in the update dialog.

articles.title: Home Assistant signs in to Renault accounts requiring an email code
articles.dek: A two-factor prompt replaces failed setup and repeated retries when the car service requires verification.
body: Home Assistant handles Renault accounts that require an emailed verification code. Setup and credential replacement ask which registered address should receive the code, then allow a mistyped code to be entered again without starting over.

Existing connections that encounter the requirement ask the owner to sign in again instead of retrying setup indefinitely. Successful verification remembers the device so later password sign-ins do not request a fresh code every time.

articles.title: Sonoff thermostat update stops midnight resets to frost protection
articles.dek: Firmware in Zigpy’s update collection also corrects temperature jumps when heating switches.
body: Firmware 1.0.5 for the Sonoff TP-WGZBA thermostat enters Zigpy’s update collection with a correction for scheduled heating falling back to five degrees Celsius at midnight. That value is the thermostat’s frost-protection setting.
The update also improves temperature compensation so switching the heating relay does not make the reported temperature jump by 0.5 to 1.6 degrees. The submitted firmware was tested on the device.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s installer lets people stop an installation
articles.dek: Drive writes can be cancelled, and virtual-machine setup can stop before creation begins.
body: Home Assistant’s installer adds a Cancel control during drive installation and the preparatory stages of Proxmox and UTM virtual-machine setup. It waits for work to stop, then explains whether nothing was written or the drive needs another installation before use. Virtual-machine cancellation ends when creation begins; a failed cleanup identifies any uploaded image that needs manual removal.

The installer also asks the operating system to prevent idle sleep during lengthy jobs while allowing the screen to turn off. Deliberate sleep remains possible, and Windows Modern Standby on battery limits how long the request holds. Cancellation has automated coverage but has not yet been verified on real drives or live virtual-machine installations.

articles.title: ESPHome controls APC gates through a local serial connection
articles.dek: Compatible sliding and swing openers report their actual position as well as accepting commands.
body: ESPHome adds local control for APC Proteous, Logico24 and Able gate openers that accept the Infinity 2.0 Wi-Fi module. A serial connection takes the module’s place and supports opening, closing, stopping and moving to a partial position.

The controller’s own status and position reports determine the displayed state. Commands that receive no acknowledgement are retried, and partial opening stops the motor when its reported position reaches the requested point.

articles.title: ESPHome automations can request power from USB-C chargers
articles.dek: An ESP32 with an FUSB302B chip can negotiate voltage and react when its supply is ready.
body: ESPHome adds USB-C Power Delivery support for makers using an ESP32 and an FUSB302B chip. A configuration requests a voltage between 5 and 20 volts; the device chooses the highest fixed voltage the charger offers that does not exceed the request.

New automations react to connection, disconnection, power readiness and communication errors, and can request a different voltage while connected. Diagnostic readings show the negotiated voltage and current allowance, rather than measuring the power a connected circuit actually consumes.

The change completes the component’s earlier protocol and chip support with the controls and status needed to use it in automations. A charger that does not complete Power Delivery negotiation leaves it at the default five volts.

articles.title: Assist answers Russian questions about rooms and floors
articles.dek: Requests can check which lights are on or whether windows and doors are closed in a chosen part of the home.
body: Assist expands Russian questions about device states to rooms and floors. The grammar recognizes requests such as which lights are on in the kitchen, whether all the lights on the first floor are off, and whether the windows on the second floor are closed.

Ruslan Alimov adds missing forms for locked doors and open windows, and corrects answers about window and opening sensors to say open or closed. This is his first contribution to the intents repository, reviewed by HepoH3.

articles.title: Music Assistant restores playback controls on older Android phones
articles.dek: Android 9 through 12 show the song and working buttons instead of an empty notification.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app restores the playback notification on Android 9 through 12. Those versions showed an empty card because the app supplied artwork but relied on newer Android behavior to fill in the song details and buttons.

Andrii Mitnovych supplies the title, artist and playback state directly, alongside previous, play or pause, and next controls. The card also mirrors up to two configured actions, such as switching players, marking a favorite or seeking.

articles.title: ESPHome connects automations to a television’s HDMI control bus
articles.dek: Makers can receive and send control messages, with higher-level device behaviour still to follow.
body: ESPHome adds a connection to HDMI-CEC, the control channel that televisions and connected equipment use to exchange commands. Makers can trigger automations from messages such as a remote’s volume button and send commands such as putting the connected equipment into standby.

This first component supplies the message transport, receiving and sending commands from configured automations. Automatic device replies and a fuller message decoder remain follow-up work. It was tested on ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3 and ESP8266 hardware.

articles.title: Home Assistant lets AI assistants find devices and automations by name
articles.dek: A search tool covers devices, areas, automations and scenes as well as entities.
body: Home Assistant adds a search tool to its large-language-model interface so a connected AI assistant can find entities, devices, areas, labels, automations, scripts and scenes by name.
Results are ranked and grouped, with up to five of each kind returned at a time. The assistant can request another page within a category instead of receiving an entire collection at once.

pullRequests.title: Add search tool to the Home Assistant LLM API

articles.title: Home Assistant sends a whole trip to a Tesla
articles.dek: Automations can pass an ordered list of stops, ending with the final destination.
body: Home Assistant adds a Tesla Fleet action for sending a multi-stop route to the car in one request. An automation can prepare a sequence such as school drop-offs followed by the office, rather than sending only one destination.

The action requires Google Place IDs for every stop; Home Assistant does not translate addresses or coordinates into those IDs. A two-stop trip was verified on a 2026 Model Y, with the stops arriving in the supplied order. This is Sabaat Ahmad’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core.
